- [Substack: FICO’s Monopoly is Fading & Consumers Are the Winners w/ Kelsey Zhu | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 59](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/ficos-monopoly-is-fading-and-consumers) - 2026-05-11

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Kelsey Zhu explains how lender choice and price differences threaten FICO's mortgage franchise. Eisman maintains his short and sketches a conditional further 40% fall; Zhu projects multi-year share and earnings pressure. They then compare information-services business models, including data networks, recurring revenue, customer demand and AI exposure. Subsequent VantageScore usage supports the competitive direction, while precise share targets and long-term AI outcomes remain open.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

### 009. FICO 10T is about ten times as expensive as VantageScore after success fees, even with only 15%-30% of applications closing.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 23:10-25:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PL5bLlPAoOk&t=1390s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The fee arithmetic can create a large premium under simplified assumptions, but a universal tenfold comparison does not follow without consistent denominators.

Conditional reasoning: Expected charge per application is 0.99 + 65 times closing probability. It is $10.74 at 15% and $20.49 at 30%; additional pulls or different funding-fee incidence change the ratio.

Assessment test: Specify pulls per application, bureau count, score fees per funded borrower and close rate. With one score per application, 0.99 + 65c equals $10.74 at c=.15 and $20.49 at c=.30; repeated pulls change the average.

- [Q2 FY2026 investor presentation, page 8](https://fico.gcs-web.com/static-files/66ef723c-1f2e-4501-a452-ab2f3d02ae85) (2026-04-28): Classic performance pricing was $4.95 per score plus $33 funding fee; 10T was $0.99 plus $65; flat per-score pricing was $10.
